Forensic Nursing Debacle

By: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A profession in peril” with a looming crisis in the nursing fraternity may leave specialised Forensic Nursing services in endless limbo.

Unique Selling Point:
There is a looming crisis within the nursing fraternity. The phasing out of the old legacy nursing programs is a cause for great concern, for specialised nursing programs. All this is happening while the South African Nursing Council, lags behind in accrediting forensic nursing before the presidential deadline, to have one nurse in each hospital by March 2020.
This story will demonstrate the ironic systematic failure between the nursing council and Department of Health and the failures to implement presidential mandate to address GBV in South Africa.
Even though we have Forensic Nurses in South Africa. The South African Nursing Council still have not accredited this specialised nursings program that enables victims of Sexual assault and other crimes come closer to finding justice.


Summary:
The South African Nursing Council is responsible for regulating all nursing qualifications, institutions and overall policy making within the nursing sector. The council however has been lagging behind in ensuring that Forensic nurses are recognised as a specialised postgraduate course and profession.

This forensic nursing postgraduate qualification was largely provided by the University of Free State, between 2011 and 2017. The university made claims to only 200 out of approximately 400 graduates of their F-Nursing program. This one year course was done outside of the SANC awarding the accreditation to the University of Freestate which has caused much warranted frustrations to the graduates of forensic nurses, some of which have more than eight to ten years working in hospitals and Thuthuzela Care Centres, around county without being accredited.
With the acknowledgement of the much needed service Forensic Nurses provided, to sexual assault victims. Cyril Ramaphosa’s GBV emergency plan, stated that by March 2020, there should be a Forensic Nurse in each hospital nationally. However, the University of free State having a majority of students coming from their school, created a conundrum, which poses the question
Firstly will the Council accredit the Forensic Nursing discipline in time to meet the March 2020 deadline?

Secondly since there has been an phasing out of old the old curriculum, and postgraduate degrees, what does it mean for the 400 plus FNurses, who graduated under an uncredited course provided by the Free State university.

Finally: What does the Regulatory body and the Minister of Health say about the All nursing postgraduate specialisation courses not being offered in 2020, and the looming gap of nursing within the public sector.


Further information:
By Speaking to a victim of sexual assault assisted by a forensic nurse, we will demonstrate how the much the country depends on forensic nurses to administer rape kits, collect evidence, and to testify in court, by providing medico legal services to victims and survivors of GBV.

We will then spend time in the day and life as a Forensic nurse and what goes into the work that these individuals, particularly when there is no doctor on duty. We will then ask that nurse give us her experiences in court, being undermined, by the justice system/police, because of the unrecognition of this course and profession. She will talk about the pain of having to work tireless hours, without the necessary compensation.

When speaking to the University of free State, who initiated the provision of the forensic nursing course in the first place. We will discuss why the university went behind the Council and taught students this one year course without accreditation of the course. We will ask how their working graduates, had a bone to pick with the university, for making them assume they would be accredited once they graduate?

We will speak to the South Africa Association of Forensic Nursing Chairperson, who will explain the very tedious, experience they have had in getting accredited. And Why they believe both the Council and the university of Freestate are liable in pushing graduates into other fields of nursing and moving to work within the private sector, or overseas.

The South African Nursing Council: Will have to speak about why they have taken so long to accredit Forensic Nursing. They will have to answer how the new curriculums now, do not include specialized programs, and postgraduate programs are still in limbo, because of the new nursing criteria, has not been drawn up, what will happen to the nurses who already have the forensic nursing an-accredited qualification.

And does the Council intend on ensuring that the President's mandate will come to fullision in March 2020.

Press Release:


Forensic Nurses in Limbo
A forensic nurse in every health facility by March 2020 – that was one of the remedies President Cyril Ramaphosa set out in his Emergency Action Plan, responding to last year’s nationwide protests against increased sexual violence. These specialised nurses can collect physical evidence, counsel rape victims and testify in court to put rapists behind bars – but only if they are duly accredited. Carte Blanche investigates why the president’s promises are far from being realised and confronts the South African Nursing Council on its failure to accredit forensic nurses.
Producer: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A profession in peril” with a looming crisis in the nursing fraternity may leave specialised Forensic Nursing services in endless limbo.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: There is a looming crisis within the nursing fraternity. The phasing out of the old legacy nursing programs is a cause for great concern, for specialised nursing programs. All this is happening while the South African Nursing Council, lags behind in accrediting forensic nursing before the presidential deadline, to have one nurse in each hospital by March 2020. This story will demonstrate the ironic systematic failure between the nursing council and Department of Health and the failures to implement presidential mandate to address GBV in South Africa. Even though we have Forensic Nurses in South Africa. The South African Nursing Council still have not accredited this specialised nursings program that enables victims of Sexual assault and other crimes come closer to finding justice.
metadata.Summary: The South African Nursing Council is responsible for regulating all nursing qualifications, institutions and overall policy making within the nursing sector. The council however has been lagging behind in ensuring that Forensic nurses are recognised as a specialised postgraduate course and profession. This forensic nursing postgraduate qualification was largely provided by the University of Free State, between 2011 and 2017. The university made claims to only 200 out of approximately 400 graduates of their F-Nursing program. This one year course was done outside of the SANC awarding the accreditation to the University of Freestate which has caused much warranted frustrations to the graduates of forensic nurses, some of which have more than eight to ten years working in hospitals and Thuthuzela Care Centres, around county without being accredited. With the acknowledgement of the much needed service Forensic Nurses provided, to sexual assault victims. Cyril Ramaphosa’s GBV emergency plan, stated that by March 2020, there should be a Forensic Nurse in each hospital nationally. However, the University of free State having a majority of students coming from their school, created a conundrum, which poses the question Firstly will the Council accredit the Forensic Nursing discipline in time to meet the March 2020 deadline? Secondly since there has been an phasing out of old the old curriculum, and postgraduate degrees, what does it mean for the 400 plus FNurses, who graduated under an uncredited course provided by the Free State university. Finally: What does the Regulatory body and the Minister of Health say about the All nursing postgraduate specialisation courses not being offered in 2020, and the looming gap of nursing within the public sector.
metadata.Further information: By Speaking to a victim of sexual assault assisted by a forensic nurse, we will demonstrate how the much the country depends on forensic nurses to administer rape kits, collect evidence, and to testify in court, by providing medico legal services to victims and survivors of GBV. We will then spend time in the day and life as a Forensic nurse and what goes into the work that these individuals, particularly when there is no doctor on duty. We will then ask that nurse give us her experiences in court, being undermined, by the justice system/police, because of the unrecognition of this course and profession. She will talk about the pain of having to work tireless hours, without the necessary compensation. When speaking to the University of free State, who initiated the provision of the forensic nursing course in the first place. We will discuss why the university went behind the Council and taught students this one year course without accreditation of the course. We will ask how their working graduates, had a bone to pick with the university, for making them assume they would be accredited once they graduate? We will speak to the South Africa Association of Forensic Nursing Chairperson, who will explain the very tedious, experience they have had in getting accredited. And Why they believe both the Council and the university of Freestate are liable in pushing graduates into other fields of nursing and moving to work within the private sector, or overseas. The South African Nursing Council: Will have to speak about why they have taken so long to accredit Forensic Nursing. They will have to answer how the new curriculums now, do not include specialized programs, and postgraduate programs are still in limbo, because of the new nursing criteria, has not been drawn up, what will happen to the nurses who already have the forensic nursing an-accredited qualification. And does the Council intend on ensuring that the President's mandate will come to fullision in March 2020.
